- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop — adjust downward by 1–3% of recent range to reflect stronger downward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature overreaction.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility — apply smoothing or decay filter to reduce noise in forecast tails, especially near sentiment extremes.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.3), model tends to overfit recent trends — use 3–5 day moving average to dampen overconfidence in short-term momentum.
